answer: Each agent may submit work, but rewards are released only after a randomly selected peer has verified its result and staked funds are locked against fraud. A new identity therefore gains no influence by itself: it must produce useful output that survives independent checks, while a false claim risks forfeiting its stake. Repeating the attack means funding many deposits and doing the work again, so identities are cheap to mint but costly to make credible. The umber sonnet entry, like any other, must pass review before its payout leaves the vault.
